title: Surjectivity of a coherent formal-system map is detected modulo the ideal
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent ideal. A morphism $(\mathcal F_n)\to(\mathcal G_n)$ in the category $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], which is abelian [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian] in the sense of [def-sp-abelian], is an epimorphism if and only if its component $\mathcal F_1\to\mathcal G_1$ is an epimorphism in the category $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 087Y (lemma-inverse-systems-surjective, line 6396); proof 'Omitted. Hint: Look on affine opens, use Lemma 087W (lemma-inverse-systems-affine) and Algebra, Lemma 00DV (algebra-lemma-NAK, Nakayama's lemma)'. 'Surjective' in an abelian category means Coker = 0 (Homology, Definition 010B), equivalently epimorphism (Lemma 010C (2)).

proof.text: Choose the cokernel cofork c of alpha given by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian]. Its image under the full inclusion followed by evaluation at each level is colimiting. Mathlib CokernelCofork.isColimitMapCoconeEquiv identifies these mapped cocones with cokernel coforks of the component maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-preadditive-epi-iff-cokernel-zero], alpha is epi iff c.pt is zero, and alpha at op 0 is epi iff c.pt at op 0 is zero.

For any sheaf of modules H and natural number n, suppose H/I^(n+1)H is zero and I^(n+2)H is zero. At each x, the power, product and quotient formulas in [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk] give J^(n+1) H_x = H_x and J^(n+2) H_x = 0, where J is the image of the ideal stalk in O_X,x. Since J^(n+1) is contained in J, J H_x = H_x. Inductively J^k H_x = H_x for every k, using (J^k J)H_x = J^k(J H_x); k=n+2 shows H_x=0. This is the elementary power-annihilated version of Stacks 00DV (9), not an assertion that J itself is nilpotent in O_X,x. For every open and section, all germs are zero because each stalk is a subsingleton. Mathlib TopCat.Presheaf.section_ext then makes the section zero. Extensionality shows the identity of H equals zero, hence H is a zero object.

For a coherent formal module C as in [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], suppose its component at op 0 is zero. Induct on n. If C_n is zero, the defining isomorphism C_(n+1)/I^(n+1)C_(n+1) = C_n makes that quotient zero; C_(n+1) is killed by I^(n+2) by the defining annihilation condition. The preceding step gives C_(n+1)=0. Thus all components are zero. Mathlib Functor.isZero makes the underlying inverse system zero; IsZero.of_full_of_faithful_of_isZero reflects this through the full inclusion.

If alpha is epi, its formal cokernel is zero by step 1, hence its first component is zero by evaluation, giving epicity of the first map. Conversely, epicity of the first map makes the first component of the formal cokernel zero by step 1; step 3 makes the formal cokernel zero, and step 1 gives epicity of alpha.

split_report.summary: Split from the hint of Stacks 087Y (proof omitted there). Step 1 reduces both sides to cokernels: in Coh(X,I) the cokernel is termwise (087X node), and epi iff cokernel zero (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-preadditive-epi-iff-cokernel-zero, Stacks 010C(2), Mathlib Preadditive.epi_iff_isZero_cokernel'), so the claim is C_1 = 0 => C_n = 0. Steps 2-4: on a Noetherian affine cover, via 087W (lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine) alpha becomes f : M -> N of finite A^-modules with alpha_n = f mod I^n; C_1 = 0 gives N = f(M) + IN, and Nakayama (lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson, 00DV(2)) with IA^ in the Jacobson radical (lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal (1), lem-weil-pbc-adic-complete-jacobson-radical) gives f surjective, hence C_n(U_j) = 0 and C_n = 0. Source tag corrected: Nakayama is Algebra 00DV (lemma-NAK), not 00MB (completion-flat). Statement unchanged except the citation [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] for the module category, added to stmt_deps. Tags 087Y, 087W, 087X, 00DV, 010B, 010C checked in tags/tags.
